title: Data Collection Without Explicit Consent
description: Continuous sensor data collection (heart rate, GPS, step counts) may occur without explicit, informed consent from the user, violating privacy principles.

title: Insufficient Notification of Data Collection
description: Users may not be adequately informed about the extent, duration, and purposes of continuous sensor data collection before wearing the device.

title: Data Used for Unintended Purposes
description: Health and location data collected may be used for purposes beyond what the user agreed to, such as insurance underwriting, marketing, or law enforcement without consent.

title: Unauthorized Data Sharing with Third Parties
description: Wearable device may share collected sensor data with third-party services (e.g., cloud providers, advertisers, insurers) without user authorization.

title: Data Breach and Unauthorized Access
description: Continuous data collection creates a persistent attack surface; collected health and location data may be exposed through security vulnerabilities or breaches.

title: Inaccurate or Incomplete Health Data
description: Sensor data quality issues may lead to inaccurate health metrics, affecting user decisions and potentially causing harm from misinterpretation of data.

title: Device ID tracking
description: Device ID transmitted to companion app enables identification and tracking of individual users across sessions and devices
assumptions: Device ID is unique to each user

title: Unauthorized data disclosure
description: GPS traces and sensor data could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties during transmission or storage
assumptions: Data transmission is not fully encrypted

title: Unintended data usage
description: Exercise session and GPS data could be used for purposes other than fitness tracking, such as insurance underwriting or marketing
assumptions: Data may be shared with third parties

title: Lack of lawful basis for data collection
description: Sensor data collection may not have adequate user consent or legal basis
assumptions: Users may not be fully informed about data collection purposes

title: Excessive data retention
description: Exercise sessions, GPS traces, and timestamps may be retained longer than necessary for the stated purpose
assumptions: Data retention policies are not clearly defined

title: Insufficient data notification
description: Users may not be adequately informed about what data is being collected and how it's being used
assumptions: Privacy policies may not be prominently displayed

title: Unintended Disclosure of Health Data
description: User's calorie, meal, and weight data could be inadvertently disclosed to unauthorized third parties through app vulnerabilities, data breaches, or improper sharing mechanisms.

title: Inaccurate User-Entered Health Data
description: Users may input incorrect calorie, meal, or weight information due to lack of validation, leading to inaccurate health tracking and potentially misleading health recommendations.

title: Insufficient Privacy Notice for Health Data Collection
description: Users may not be adequately informed about how their sensitive health data will be collected, stored, and shared, potentially violating transparency requirements.

title: Legal Basis for Health Data Collection Unclear
description: The app may lack clear legal justification for collecting sensitive health data, potentially violating GDPR or other privacy regulations.

title: Inadequate Data Destruction of User Health Data
description: User health data may not be properly destroyed when no longer needed or when user requests deletion, leading to residual data exposure.

title: Excessive Health Data Collection
description: The companion mobile app may collect more health data (calorie intake, weight history, exercise sessions) than necessary for the intended purpose, violating data minimization principles.

title: Inaccurate Health Data Storage
description: Health logs written to the data store may contain inaccurate or incomplete information, which could lead to incorrect health assessments or medical decisions.

title: Health Data Re-identification Risk
description: The combination of health logs (calorie intake, weight history, exercise sessions) may be sufficiently unique to re-identify individuals, especially when combined with other data sources.

title: Non-compliant Health Data Storage
description: The health log store may not comply with applicable privacy regulations (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR) for storing sensitive health information.

title: Insufficient User Notice
description: Users may not be adequately informed about what health data is being collected, how it will be used, and with whom it may be shared.

title: Unlawful Data Collection
description: The collection and storage of health logs may lack proper legal authorization or consent from users, violating privacy laws.

title: Inadequate Data Destruction
description: The health log store may not have proper policies for data retention and destruction, leading to unnecessary long-term storage of sensitive health information.

title: Location data collected without explicit consent
description: GPS location traces are collected and written to the location history store without clear indication of user consent or privacy notice.
assumptions: Assumes the app collects location data from the device.

title: Location data stored without encryption
description: GPS location traces are stored in the location history store without encryption, making them vulnerable to unauthorized access.
assumptions: Assumes the store does not implement encryption at rest.

title: Sensitive location patterns inferred
description: Location history traces can be analyzed to infer sensitive information about user habits, movements, and personal routines.
assumptions: Assumes location data can be analyzed for pattern inference.

title: Location data disclosed to unauthorized parties
description: Location history stored in DS2 could be accessed by unauthorized parties through data breaches or unauthorized access.
assumptions: Assumes DS2 is accessible to unauthorized parties.

title: Unintended third-party access to location data
description: Location data stored in DS2 may be accessed by third parties who should not have access to this sensitive information.
assumptions: Assumes DS2 is not properly secured against third-party access.

title: Unauthorized Access to Health Logs
description: Health logs containing calorie, weight, and exercise data are stored in DS1 and may be accessed by unauthorized parties during storage or transfer to P3.

title: Excessive Data Collection Across Sessions
description: The analytics service reads health logs across multiple sessions, potentially collecting more data than necessary for health-condition analysis, violating data minimization principles.

title: Insufficient User Notification
description: Users may not be adequately informed that their health data is being used for health-condition analysis across sessions, violating notification requirements.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance for Health Data Processing
description: Processing of sensitive health data for analytics may not comply with applicable privacy regulations (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR) without proper legal basis and safeguards.

title: Processing without adequate legal basis
description: Location history may be processed for health analytics without sufficient legal basis or explicit consent from users.

title: Excessive location data collection
description: Location history across all sessions may be collected beyond what is strictly necessary for deriving daily routine and movement patterns.

title: Excessive data retention
description: Location history may be retained longer than necessary for health analytics purposes, increasing privacy risk.

title: Inaccurate location data
description: Health analytics derived from location history may be inaccurate due to data quality issues, leading to incorrect routine and pattern analysis.

title: Unintended access to location data
description: Location history processed by health analytics service may be accessed by unauthorized parties or system administrators.

title: Lack of notification to users
description: Users may not be adequately informed that their location history is being used to derive health analytics and movement patterns.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Sensitive Health Information
description: Health condition risk indicators and inferred health insights may be disclosed to unauthorized parties or in an unauthorized manner during transmission from analytics service to companion app.

title: Inaccurate or Misleading Health Insights
description: Inferred health insights (risk indicators, trend flags) may be inaccurate or misleading, potentially causing users to make incorrect health decisions based on flawed analytics.

title: Unintended Access to Health Analytics Data
description: Companion mobile app may have unintended access to health analytics data, or data may be accessible to unauthorized users within the app environment.

title: Lack of Control Over Data Sharing
description: Analytics service may lack proper controls over how health insights are shared with the companion app, potentially leading to excessive or inappropriate data exposure.

title: Insufficient notice about health data display
description: Users may not be adequately informed about what health-related indicators (eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals) are being displayed on the app dashboard, and how this information is being used or shared.
assumptions: Users may not fully understand the implications of health data being displayed on their dashboard.

title: Questionable legitimacy of health indicator display
description: The legitimacy of displaying inferred health condition indicators to users may be questionable without clear justification, proper consent, or regulatory approval for this specific health-related data processing.
assumptions: Users may not have given explicit consent for health-related data to be displayed in this manner.

title: Potential inappropriate use of health data
description: Health-related indicators displayed to users may be used beyond their intended purpose (e.g., for marketing, profiling, or third-party sharing) without user knowledge or consent.
assumptions: The app may have broader data usage policies that extend beyond the dashboard display functionality.

title: Excessive data collection for analytics
description: Health Analytics Service may collect and transfer more health and location data than necessary for the analytics purpose, violating data minimization principles.

title: Data integrity risk during replication
description: Third-party cloud hosting provider may experience data corruption, loss, or unauthorized modification during data replication, compromising data integrity of health and location datasets.

title: Insufficient anonymization of health data
description: Health and location data stored at cloud provider may not be adequately anonymized or de-identified, creating re-identification risks for individuals.

title: Legal basis for data processing unclear
description: Health Analytics Service may not have clear legal basis or appropriate consent for transferring and storing sensitive health data at third-party cloud provider.

title: Non-compliance with data protection regulations
description: Third-party cloud hosting provider may not be fully compliant with applicable data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA) regarding health data storage and replication.
